value.body: Questioned document examiners study signatures, handwriting, printing, inks and paper to find out whether a document is genuine or altered. Private forensic labs, independent examiners, banks and insurers, and law firms rely on them in property, banking and fraud disputes. The work is detailed bench analysis followed by a written opinion.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Forensic Science, often with an M.Sc

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Stereo microscopes, video spectral comparators, UV/IR light sources

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually train under an experienced examiner or in a private forensic lab, since judgement builds with supervised casework. Courts treat the report as expert opinion, so methods and reasoning need to hold up under cross-examination.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Use of optical and imaging instruments

value.title: At a glance
items: Training under supervision is long before independent reporting.
Private practice depends on reputation and referrals.
Next steps: senior examiner, lab lead, or independent practice.
